steps.title: What concatenation needs
steps.body: Link $\text{tail}(L_1)\to\text{head}(L_2)$ and, to keep a proper list, connect $\text{tail}(L_2)$ back to $\text{head}(L_1)$. Finding the tails must be O(1).

steps.title: Circular doubly linked list
steps.body:
With only head pointers, $\text{tail}=\text{head.prev}$ in O(1) for both lists. A constant number of pointer updates splices them:

```
t1 = h1.prev; t2 = h2.prev
t1.next = h2; h2.prev = t1
t2.next = h1; h1.prev = t2
```

Arrays need copying of $L_2$ (O(n)) and possibly reallocation.

pitfalls: If explicit tail pointers were kept, other lists could work too — the standard representation keeps only the head.

cse-1997-a-6.approach: Left recursion makes an operator left-associative; right recursion makes it right-associative.

steps.body: $X\to X\oplus Y$: the recursive non-terminal $X$ is on the **left**, so $a\oplus b\oplus c$ parses as $(a\oplus b)\oplus c$ — left associative.

steps.title: Rule for ⊙
steps.body: $Y\to Z\odot Y$: the recursive $Y$ is on the **right**, so $a\odot b\odot c$ parses as $a\odot(b\odot c)$ — right associative.

⊙'s production is right-recursive, so it is not left associative.
